title: Before Egypt by Robert Bloch - Audiobook
author: Dream audio books
description:
Before Egypt by Robert Bloch is a fast-moving science-fiction adventure that blends ancient mystery, interplanetary travel, danger, and speculation about the origins of civilization.
The story follows Mike Mallison, a capable big-game guide who accepts one of the strangest assignments of his career. Professor Brandon and his daughter Doree are convinced that an ancient papyrus may contain evidence linking early Egyptian civilization to a distant world. What begins as an unusual expedition quickly becomes a dangerous journey far beyond Earth.
Their search takes them toward a remote planet in the Orion sector, where the mystery surrounding ancient Egypt becomes even more extraordinary. Along the way, Mallison and his companions face betrayal, kidnapping, hostile environments, and rivals determined to exploit the secret for themselves. The deeper the expedition goes, the more the line between archaeology and science fiction begins to disappear.
Bloch builds the story around an irresistible question: what if part of humanity’s ancient past had an extraterrestrial connection? Instead of treating Egypt simply as a historical setting, the tale transforms it into the starting point for a much larger cosmic mystery.
Adventure remains at the heart of the story. Mallison must rely on courage, quick thinking, and determination as the expedition becomes increasingly dangerous, while the mystery of the ancient evidence continues to pull the characters forward.
Originally associated with the January 1957 issue of Amazing Stories, Before Egypt is an entertaining example of mid-century pulp science fiction, combining lost-civilization ideas with space adventure and archaeological mystery.
This audiobook is ideal for listeners who enjoy classic science fiction, ancient mysteries, alien worlds, exploration, and vintage pulp adventure.

Audit This finds that moment.

One story an episode, followed all the way to the end of it. Frauds, collapses,
cost blowouts, contracts, cover ups, and the occasional thing that everybody
accepted as true because nobody went and looked.

Every episode is built from the record: court transcripts, sentencing remarks,

No speculation. No dramatisation. No guessing at what anyone was thinking. Just

title: How do you choose the best IPTV service?
author: Ban Stock
description:
I've been researching the best IPTV options lately, and one thing I've noticed is that almost every provider makes the same promises: thousands of channels, HD/4K quality, sports, movies, VOD, and “no buffering.” It can be difficult to know which features actually matter.

👉 🚀 Try the Best IPTV Experience Today — Explore the Official IPTV Trial

Personally, I think channel count shouldn't be the main deciding factor. I'd rather have a smaller selection that works consistently than thousands of channels with broken streams or duplicate content.Some of the things I'd check before choosing an IPTV service are:
  • Streaming stability: Does it continue working smoothly during busy evening hours?
  • Picture quality: Is the actual quality good, rather than just advertising 4K?
  • EPG: Are program names and schedules accurate?
  • Device support: Does it work properly on your TV, streaming device, phone, or computer?
  • VOD library: If movies and shows are important, are they organized and playable?
  • Customer support: Can you get a useful response when something goes wrong?
  • Pricing: Are renewal costs and subscription terms clearly explained?
  • Cancellation/refunds: Are the policies easy to understand?
  • Content rights: Does the provider have authorization to distribute the channels and content it offers?
I've also seen people recommend IPTV providers on forums and Reddit, but I think those recommendations should be taken with some caution. A short post saying “this is the best IPTV” doesn't tell you much.

👉 🚀 Try the Best IPTV Experience Today — Explore the Official IPTV Trial

A detailed review explaining how long someone has used a service, what device they use, their location, and how the service performs during peak hours is much more useful.Another thing I'd avoid is immediately paying for a very long subscription.

If a legitimate provider offers a trial or short-term plan, testing it first seems like a safer way to see whether it actually meets your needs.For anyone here who has experience with IPTV, what do you think is the most important factor when choosing a service?

Is it reliability, sports coverage, VOD, channel selection, price, or something else?I'm interested in hearing actual user experiences rather than promotional recommendations.

title: Side B: The Deeper Cut, Daily
author: Cam Tait
description:
SIDE B — Episode 1: The Origin Story.

Fifty years ago, a thirteen-year-old kid sat on a basement floor in Edmonton, listening to 630 CHED Radio. A gentleman named Bob Comfort came on the air — and nothing was ever quite the same after that.Bob had a segment called Posters for Your Mind.

He'd take the week's top song and pull the human story out of it. It was unlike anything I'd heard. And sitting there, I thought: maybe I can do that.What followed was a broadcasting course, a record collection full of scratches, and an instructor who — wisely — kept me fifty feet from the turntable.That was almost fifty years ago.
The equipment has changed. The dream hasn't.
This is Episode 1 of Side B. It's my origin story — why this podcast exists, what took so long, and what's finally made it possible. Including a part about cerebral palsy I don't talk around.
Every episode ends with a song. This one closes with Trisha Yearwood."The Song Remembers When."It'll make sense when you hear it.
Welcome to Side B. Pull up a chair.

Welcome to "Ask the Guitar Coach" - the ONLY podcast where all your guitar learning questions are answered!

title: L.O.K.i.
author: just_loki
description:
L.O.K.i. is a podcast about the truths we avoid, the identities we inherit, the relationships that shape us, and the work of becoming who we actually are. Through reflection, philosophy, personal observation, healing, self-worth, and uncomfortable truths, just_loki explores the parts of life we often feel but struggle to put into words.
This is a mirror, not a lecture. A place to question what you’ve accepted, recognize what is truly yours, and define yourself beyond expectation, illusion, and conformity.
Liberate. Observe. Know. Integrate.
See Yourself. Become Yourself.

author: WeAreEmmanuel

Tune in for a lot of heart, a lot of laughs, and a lot of gospel truths as these two share resources and their heart for Emmanuel.

author: Melissa Kish
description:
Welcome to The Pet Tea Podcast, your weekly source for all things pets, from product must-haves to the latest industry drama! Join us as we spill the ultimate tea on everything happening in the world of pets!



Listening will uncover:

author: City Cast
description: Seattle is booming, and expensive, and full of people trying to figure out how to build a life here that actually works. Weaving Our Future: Stories for a Fair Economy is a five-part City Cast Partner Studios series about the people doing exactly that, organizing, building coalitions, and pushing for the policy changes that decide whether King County's economy works for everyone or just the people already winning. Across five episodes, City Cast Seattle host Jane C. Hu talks with the advocates and coalition leaders closest to the work: fixing how Washington funds early learning and K-12 schools, building parent and community political power from the ground up, fighting for progressive revenue and the Millionaire's Tax against a well-funded repeal effort, protecting people from homelessness while defending the housing progress already made, and reimagining what dignity and ownership look like for workers across the region. Every episode is a different piece of the same puzzle,  what it actually takes to build a fair economy in King County, told through the people building it. Subscribe now so you don't miss a single conversation.

title: Deck Builders Myrtle Beach

title: Who Hit My Stop Sign?

title: Dear Aunty with Aunty Charmaine

description:
Dear Aunty | A Podcast + Advice Column by Soultribe Media


Hey Soultribe. It's your Aunty Charmaine — and I am so glad you found your way here.


Dear Aunty is not your average podcast. This is a sanctuary. This is the place where real letters from real people meet real wisdom, real truth, and real love — every single Friday.

You share what is weighing on you — the financial stress, the generational patterns, the relationships that cost you more than they gave, the habits you never learned, the life you are trying to build without a blueprint. I am Aunty Charmaine — spiritual life coach, psychic medium, shamanic healer, ancestral healing guide, and HuffPost contributor. Every episode lives inside a larger monthly theme rooted in the real cost of living — not just financially, but spiritually, ancestrally, and communally. Because the truth is, healing does not happen in just one area of your life. It happens across all of them, all at once.


New episodes drop every Friday on Buzzsprout, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and soultribe.media.


Ready to submit your letter to Dear Aunty? Head to soultribe.media and let Aunty know what is on your heart. Your story is safe here. Your identity stays protected. Always.


And if this podcast has ever made you feel seen, supported, or less alone — subscribe, share it with someone who needs it, and come join us deeper inside the Soultribe on Patreon. We are building something real over there.


Welcome home, sweetheart. Aunty has been waiting for you.


— Aunty Charmaine

title: Quake
author: Shahid Amin Traveler71
description:
Quake tells the true stories of the world's great earthquakes and tsunamis and the science of how the Earth moves. Each episode, host Nirob takes one earthquake — a city that fell on a holy day and shook the faith of a continent, a harbour that burned for three days, a wave that crossed an ocean in a night and killed a quarter of a million people, a nuclear power station overwhelmed by the sea — and rebuilds it: the fault beneath the ground and the people who lived on it, the warnings that were or were not read, the shaking as it actually happened second by second, the aftermath of fire and flood and collapse, and the science and the building codes that came out of the ruins.

From Lisbon in 1755 to San Francisco in 1906, from Tokyo in 1923 to Tangshan in 1976, from the Indian Ocean tsunami of 2004 to Haiti, Tōhoku and the earthquakes of our own decade, Quake is about the most sudden and least predictable force in the natural world — and about how human beings learned to build for a ground that will not stay still. Meticulously researched, honest about what the science knows and what it still cannot predict, and clear about the difference between the record and the legend. Clean and suitable for all ages. A new earthquake every week

description:
College football isn’t just games. It’s drama, gossip, power struggles, NIL chaos, coaching soap operas, and personalities that refuse to stay on the field. This show lives in that space.Hosted by longtime sports-talk veteran Jared Stillman and former NFL offensive lineman and national media voice Geoff Schwartz, Jared Stillman and Geoff Schwartz’s College Football Show is a one-hour podcast that treats the sport like the unfiltered entertainment product it actually is. Think the energy of classic drive-time talk radio mixed with the insider access of someone who’s played the game and the fearlessness of hosts who aren’t trying to be everyone’s favorite analyst. They recap the biggest storylines, preview what’s coming, and spend most of their time on the stuff other shows dance around: coaching intrigue, conference politics, player and coach personalities, behind-the-scenes friction, and the takes that make people argue. 
Jared Stillman is a Nashville native and one of the most recognizable sports-talk voices in the city. He spent a decade hosting afternoon drive at 102.5 The Game, first as co-host of Jared and the GM with late Tennessee Titans general manager Floyd Reese, then as host of Stillman & Company. The show became a destination for Titans coverage, SEC football, and unapologetic local-and-national sports talk. After leaving the station in 2025, he relaunched Stillman & Co. as a daily on-demand show and continues to appear on SiriusXM’s Mad Dog Sports Radio. Stillman is known for passionate, against-the-grain opinions, a deep feel for what fans actually care about, and a style that doesn’t sand down the edges.Geoff Schwartz played eight NFL seasons as an offensive lineman for the Carolina Panthers, Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs, New York Giants, and Detroit Lions after starring at the University of Oregon, where he was a second-team All-Pac-10 selection. Since retiring, he has built a national media career as a host and analyst on SiriusXM (including NFL Radio and Mad Dog Sports Radio), FOX Sports Radio, and FOX Sports, where he also contributes betting and football analysis. He hosts Geoff Schwartz Is Smarter Than You / the Schwartz Football Show and co-authored Eat My Schwartz with his brother, former NFL tackle Mitchell Schwartz. Schwartz brings locker-room perspective, sharp scheme and personnel insight, and a dry, irreverent sense of humor.
Social Links: Jared can be found on X- @JaredStillman, IG- @TheJaredStillman
Geoff can be found on X- @GeoffSchwartz and IG- @GeoffSchwartz

title: reIMAGED: Bringing Pro Life Into Gospel Focus
author: LIFE International
description:
What if being pro-life is bigger than a political label, without making abortion just one issue among many?

Around 73 million induced abortions take place worldwide each year. Behind every number is a human being made in the image of God, and a mother, father, family, church, and community touched by abortion.

reIMAGED invites the Church to return to Scripture and recover a richer understanding of human life, human value, and Christian obedience. The right to life is the first right, the one on which every other human right depends. Christians should care about every way people are denied, discarded, or devalued, but not every issue is morally equivalent. A fuller biblical foundation does not make abortion less central. It helps us understand why abortion matters so profoundly.

Hosted by Chris and Alissa, reIMAGED brings together pastors, theologians, medical professionals, Christian leaders, ministry practitioners, global voices, and people with lived experience. The foundation is firm, but the conversation is open: How can the Church understand and live these truths more faithfully?

A podcast from LIFE International, reIMAGED is a space for honest, courageous, and compassionate conversations that bring pro-life into gospel focus.

What’s next?

title: The Church Communications Podcast by CloudCut

From faith transitions to jaw-dropping realities, I share my raw experiences, deconstruct Mormon beliefs, and explore healing after leaving high-demand religion. Whether you’re questioning, ex-Mormon, or just curious, welcome to Mormon Gone Rogue—where nothing is off-limits!

title: Loan Originator Pulse
author: MMI One
description:
What's actually working for loan officers right now? The Loan Originator Pulse goes straight to the people who know — top originators and industry voices in the trenches — for the real tactics behind today's numbers.


Each episode digs into the plays, tools, and habits driving production in this market: where the best leads are coming from, what's changed, and what to try next. title: Then, Now, Next
author: Annika Allen
description:
70 years of Black British television, told by the people who built it.


Then, Now, Next traces seven decades of Black British life on screen; from the first Black reporter on screen, Barbara Blake Hannah and the racist caricatures of The Black and White Minstrel Show, through Channel 4's multicultural unit who had £8M to spend on Black and Asian programming, the era defining Desmond's, and the rise of Black women as commissioners and show runners, the popularity of music television, including MTV's The Lick, to the making of today's Black led shows such as Supacell and Dreaming Whilst Black.


Host Annika Allen Gray (All3Media's Head of Diversity) talks to the presenters, producers and commissioners, who fought for space on the small screen, and the ones now building their own platforms instead of waiting for a green light. Each episode moves through a different chapter: the fight to be seen, the fight to be heard, and the fight to own the story.


Featured in this series are: Trisha Goddard, Richard Blackwood, Tamara Howe, June Sarpong, Sheila Nortley, Trevor Nelson, Shurwin Beckford, Trix Worrell, Sarah Asante and many more.


The 8 episode series launches on 16th September.


You can watch the interviews with the contributors in full in the Black Leaders in TV YouTube Channel.


For more information visit blackleadersintv.com/ and follow us on Instagram @blackleadersintv


Then, Now, Next is funded by the Royal Television Society's Shiers Trust Award.


Hosted by Annika Allen Gray (@annikaallen) and produced by Leanne Alie (@leannealie).

Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.

title: Let 'Em Know
author: Angela Milano
description: For the ones who've lived it and aren't afraid to say it. Let 'Em Know is a space for honest conversations about the real stuff, the moments that change us, stretch us, and wake us up. What started as The Focus Within has evolved into something bolder, more true to where host Angela is now, and where so many of us find ourselves: in the messy, beautiful middle of life, catching up to who we've already become. Through unfiltered solo episodes and deep, meaningful interviews, Angela gets into the re-choosing, the parts of yourself you inherited versus the ones you're finally picking on purpose. No scripts. Just truth. If you're in a season of figuring it out, starting over, or simply want to hear something real, you're in the right place. So pull up a seat and turn it up, because it's time to let 'em know.

title: Next Play Media Podcast
author: The Pod Mill
description: Next Play Media is building a new kind of connection in youth sports — one that brings players, parents, and the community into the same conversation. Through honest interviews with kids and their families, the show captures what actually happens on the field, in the car ride home, and around the dinner table. Local businesses and supporters don’t just put a banner on the fence; they step into the story and help strengthen the team. The result is a podcast that turns youth sports from a sideline experience into a shared community one.

title: Lead The Moment
author: William  Lewis
description:
The hardest part of leadership isn't getting the position—it's becoming the leader people need once you have it.
Hosted by Dr. Will Lewis, Lead the Moment explores the real moments that test leaders: difficult conversations, tough decisions, unexpected setbacks, and times of uncertainty. Through candid conversations and practical insights, each episode helps leaders learn to pause, assess, and respond with greater clarity, courage, and confidence.
Real Moments. Real Leadership. Real Impact.

title: Mixed: Stories and Strategies for Multiracial and Interfaith Families
author: Axis Mundi Media + IRMCE
description:
From the Institute for Religion, Media, and Civic Engagement ( IRMCE ( http://www.irmce.org ) ), and Asian Pacific American Religions Research Initiative ( APARRI ( https://aparri.org/ ) ), Mixed is a podcast about forming strong mixed race and mixed faith families and relationships. Mixed people - especially mixed kids with multiple ethnic, racial and religious identities - experience marginalization and acceptance in ways that are different from monoracial and religious minorities. But, there are simple and straightforward things people can do to make sure mixed kids and adults have a sense of belonging and pride in their backgrounds.
*Creator:* Dr. Khyati Y. Joshi ( https://www.khyatijoshi.com/ ) is a scholar-storyteller who bridges research, lived experience, and practical wisdom. She is a tenured, Full Professor in the School of Education at Fairleigh Dickinson University and the author of White Christian Privilege: The Illusion of Religious Equality in America (NYU Press, 2020) and several other books on race and religion in America.
Dr. Joshi is also part of a mixed marriage. Along with her husband John, they have raised their son to be Hindu and Christian; and to recognize, cherish, and embody his Indian and European heritages.
In this series, she blends scholarly expertise with her unique story, relaying the mistakes she’s made, the wisdom she’s gained, and the practical tips she can offer for cultivating mixed relationships and raising kids and adults to embrace their whole selves.

title: Bald Legal

description: Bald Legal cuts through the noise with candid conversations about the law, the cases shaping our world, and how the legal system actually works. Clear answers, sharp analysis, real stories, and no unnecessary legalese.

title: Foil Life Podcast
author: Foil Life Podcast Team
description: Welcome to the Foil Life Podcast, the official podcast of the Foiling Magazine! Join us as we dive into the exhilarating world of foiling. We cover wing, kite foiling, pump foiling, surf foiling, e-foiling, wake foiling, and downwind SUP foiling—plus the dynamic art of wing foiling. From expert tips and inspiring stories of athletes, innovators, and passionate riders to gear release and review episodes where we talk with top brands about the latest innovations hitting the market, we’re your ultimate source for all things foil. Whether you’re honing your skills, planning epic foil adventures, or geeking out on cutting-edge gear, tune in for unmatched stoke and insights.

title: The Peripatetics
author: Trey Hill
description: The Peripatetics is a bi-weekly podcast hosted by writer, director and avid morning walker, Trey Hill. Taking inspiration from Aristotle, we are walking toward a more tranquil life via that pathways of literature, art and philosophy.

title: The Famager Podcast
author: Famager
description:
Music Takes More Than Music.
The Famager Podcast is about the work that happens around the music: releases, shows, promotion, websites, tools, technology, organization, decisions, and all the things musicians and the people supporting them end up figuring out along the way.
Hosted by Daniel Garcia, founder of Famager, the podcast draws on real experience supporting Holden Garcia Music while also bringing in useful perspectives, ideas, and conversations from others doing the work.
There is rarely one perfect way to handle any of it. The goal is to help you understand your options, learn from other people’s experiences, ask better questions, and make decisions that fit your situation.
Whether you support someone else’s music or manage the work around your own, you’re welcome here.
Learn more at famager.com.

title: Gospel & Gratitude | A Bible Study Podcast

Hello! Welcome to the Gospel & Gratitude Podcast where we will read the Gospels entirely, revealing important themes and guide our understanding. 


Thank you for listening!

title: The Unscripted Symphony
author: Jill Fratianne
description:
Life doesn’t follow a script, and the best stories rarely go according to plan.


The Unscripted Symphony, hosted by Jill Fratianne, is about the real stories, raw moments, unexpected turns, and defining experiences that shape who we become. 


Through honest conversations with entrepreneurs, leaders, creatives, and fascinating people from all walks of life, Jill goes beyond the highlight reel to uncover the setbacks, breakthroughs, relationships, risks, and lessons that happen behind the scenes.


Each episode explores what it really looks like to navigate success, failure, reinvention, relationships, personal growth, and everything in between—with plenty of laughter and perspective along the way.


Because life isn’t about playing every note perfectly. 


It’s about showing up, embracing the unexpected, and keeping the music going.


Real stories. Raw moments. Welcome to The Unscripted Symphony.

title: The Stable Man Podcast

No Blueprint is a podcast about how baseball players actually develop — not the myth of a single "right way," but the real, individualized process behind growth.

No perfect formula guarantees outcomes in youth sports. Not for a player chasing the next level. Not for a parent trying to support their kid through it. Not for a coach building a program. Development isn't a script you follow — it's a process you navigate, and it looks different for everyone.

Each episode features honest conversations with coaches, players, leaders, and performance experts who've lived that process firsthand — the setbacks, the detours, and what actually worked. No highlight reels, no hot takes, no guaranteed formulas. Just real perspective for players, parents, and the coaches supporting them.

No blueprint. Just development.

The private habits, the specific decisions, the mentors nobody credits, the dark parts of the story that usually get left out. Output is visible. The thinking behind it isn't. author: Shawn + Beauty
description:
Love Within the Transition: Discovering Yourself While Loving Another is a podcast centered on Black queer love, relationships, and the transformative journey of loving through life’s transitions.


Inspired by our lived experience; a cisgender Black woman and a Black transgender man whose relationship evolves through gender transition. We create space for the conversations our community does not always get to have. We explore how identity, intimacy, communication, family, culture, and love evolves when one partner transitions, and how both people are transformed in the process.


Too often, the Black experiences of queer couples, and especially relationships involving Black trans men, are overlooked, misunderstood, or left out of the conversation. We are here to change that.


This show is a space where Black queer partners, trans men, and our broader community can hear honest stories, ask difficult questions, and find language for the experiences they have carried in silence. Together, we will explore what it means to support one another, nurture yourself, while building relationships rooted in authenticity, compassion, and growth.


Because loving someone through transition is not only about witnessing who they are becoming, it is also about discovering who you are.


Welcome to Love Within the Transition, where healing begins, truth is spoken, and love has room to grow.

title: Seasoned by Salt
author: Danielle Duhon
description:
Welcome to Seasoned by Salt.


Here's something most security teams aren't ready to say out loud.


AI agents are already running inside your organization. Talking to your APIs. Making decisions. Taking actions. And most security programs have no idea what those agents are actually doing.


Most AI security stops at the model. Attacks don't.


Every AI agent your organization deploys touches APIs. Those connections are where trust breaks down, where data walks out the door, and where attackers find the gaps your tools were never built to see. And the window between "deployed" and "exploited" is getting shorter every quarter.


That's exactly why we built this show.


Seasoned by Salt is the podcast where security leaders, CTOs, CISOs, and the builders behind the world's most critical platforms have the conversations that matter. No spin. No vendor theater. No surface-level takes on a problem that is anything but surface-level.


We go deep on agentic AI risk. On MCP servers, shadow APIs, and the attack surface that grows every time your organization ships something new. On the decisions that protected companies and the ones that left the door open.


Because in agentic AI security, experience is not optional. It is everything.

I'm your host, and this is Seasoned by Salt, brought to you by Salt Security, the only holistic AI security solution for the entire agentic AI lifecycle.


Subscribe now. The conversation starts here.

Welcome to Focus Reset, your regular sanctuary for clarity, mindfulness, and personal growth. Hosted by Alia, this solo-show podcast is designed for anyone looking to silence the external noise, step away from the daily hustle, and hit the reset button on their mind.

description: Welcome to Cesar's Journals, a personal audio journal hosted by Cesar Hirwa. If you want to learn how to live a free life, find true happiness, and navigate a complicated world, this solo podcast is for you. Through vulnerable personal stories, I explore what it really means to practice self-love, conquer modern fears, and master self-overcoming. From discussing why the world is default bad to learning how to set baseline boundaries, subscribe for honest weekly reflections on shifting your mindset and learning how to finally be happy.

title: BDF Insights

Business development for technical and professional services firms, and where their markets are heading.

Most engineering and consulting firms grow on delivery and reputation until that stops being enough: the work is good, the relationships are real, and growth still depends on whoever has time for it. BDF Insights looks at what makes growth deliberate. It also looks further out, at reading a market early enough to position before a shift becomes a tender.

Frans Oosthuizen is the founder of BDF Partners. After a international career in Europe, Russia and Africa, he now works with owner-led firms that sell expertise and judgement.

title: Girl, Let Me Tell You... I'm Still Here
author: Carrie Whitehead
description:
Girl, Let Me Tell You... I'm Still Here is a podcast about grief, faith, life, and everything in between.
I'm Carrie—a mom, a nurse, an author, and a woman who has learned what it means to keep living after unimaginable loss.
After losing my daughter, Lezlie, in 2015, I discovered that grief doesn't follow a timeline, and you never simply "get over" losing someone you love. But I've also learned that heartbreak doesn't mean life has to end.
Here, we'll talk about grief and loss, faith, motherhood, relationships, nursing, getting older, finding joy again, the hard stuff, the funny stuff, and...

title: Monorails and Mouse Ears
author: Jeff from JATravels.net
description:

title: Enneagram for Educators

description:

author: Podily
description:
The Political Campaign Podcast explores the strategy, organization, messaging, fundraising, and field operations behind running for office and winning elections. Designed for candidates, campaign managers, political consultants, staffers, volunteers, activists, and anyone interested in how modern campaigns actually work, the show examines the decisions that shape campaigns from the first exploratory conversations through Election Day. Episodes cover campaign planning, candidate positioning, voter targeting, opposition research, endorsements, media strategy, debate preparation, polling, fundraising, budgeting, staffing, compliance, digital advertising, and the day-to-day realities of building a competitive political operation.

The podcast also dives deep into voter contact and turnout strategy, including GOTV, canvassing, phone banking, texting, direct mail, volunteer recruitment, field offices, voter registration, data analytics, persuasion, coalition building, grassroots organizing, earned media, social media, campaign events, rapid response, crisis communications, and election-night operations. Episodes examine how campaigns use voter files, polling, demographics, fundraising data, geographic targeting, message testing, and political technology to identify supporters, persuade undecided voters, allocate resources, and maximize turnout. The show also looks at the roles played by campaign managers, communications directors, finance teams, field organizers, consultants, pollsters, media buyers, political parties, PACs, donors, volunteers, and outside organizations.

From city council and school board races to mayoral, legislative, congressional, gubernatorial, and presidential campaigns, The Political Campaign Podcast examines what candidates and campaign teams need to understand before asking voters for their support. Topics include deciding whether to run, building a campaign team, developing a winning message, raising money, managing a candidate’s schedule, navigating political attacks, preparing for debates, communicating with the press, organizing supporters, complying with election rules, surviving the final weeks of a race, and learning from both successful and unsuccessful campaigns. Whether you are considering running for office, working on a campaign, studying political strategy, or simply fascinated by elections, the podcast provides an in-depth look at the people, systems, tactics, and decisions behind modern political campaigns.

What really happens behind the businesses, systems, strategies, and decisions that shape the world around us?

Welcome to Business Uncovered, a documentary-style business podcast that explores how businesses actually work beneath the surface.

Every episode takes a closer look at the hidden mechanics of modern business from supply chains and distribution networks to franchising, manufacturing, subscriptions, logistics, retail, technology, pricing structures, marketplaces, customer journeys, business operations, and the systems that allow companies to serve millions of people.

Instead of simply telling the story of a successful company, Business Uncovered asks a different question: What is happening underneath the business?

How does a supermarket make money from thousands of products? Why do airlines operate with such complicated pricing? How can a free product become a billion-dollar business? Why do some companies rely on franchises while others own every location? What makes a business model difficult to copy? And how can a seemingly simple operation become a powerful business system?

Each episode breaks down one fascinating business mechanism, industry practice, or commercial system and explains it through clear storytelling, real-world examples, research, and practical analysis.

You don't need an MBA to understand business.

Business Uncovered turns complicated business concepts into engaging stories that reveal the systems most people never notice.

Whether you're an entrepreneur, business owner, executive, marketer, student, creator, or simply curious about how the commercial world works, this podcast will help you see everyday businesses from a completely different perspective.

No boring lectures. No business jargon for the sake of jargon.

Just fascinating business questions, surprising explanations, and clear insights into the systems behind modern commerce.

Because once you understand how the system works, you start seeing business differently.

description:
Last year, Verna and I joked about starting a podcast where we could record all the things we have to say. At the time, it was a dream rooted in humor—because really, who has the time?

But why a podcast, you ask?

As sisters, Verna and I have always connected through conversation. We have shared life as sisters, mothers, and women, navigating all the joys, challenges, and unexpected adventures that come our way. No matter the distance between us—whether it was when I left for college, when she met her soulmate and got married, when we went from being a ten-minute walk apart to a four-hour drive, and now an entire ocean away—we have always found our way back to each other through storytelling.

We talk almost every day.

You might wonder what we could possibly have left to talk about. The truth is, when it comes to storytelling, the content is endless. There is always a new memory to revisit, a lesson to unpack, a moment to celebrate, or something hilarious to laugh about. And let's be honest—there is always something to laugh about.

So here we are, finally bringing that dream to life and creating a space where we can do what we love most: talk story.

This fall, we'll launch our inaugural podcast, Storytelling Circles: A Story for a Story. Each episode will be an invitation into our circle as we share stories, reflections, laughter, and conversations that connect us across the ocean. We'll also welcome guests to join us, bringing their own stories and experiences to the circle.

We invite you to listen in, where every story finds a place in an unending circle—and where two sisters, separated by an ocean, stay connected through storytelling, laughter, and the simple joy of sharing life together.

Now, a small disclaimer: we are novice podcasters and completely inexperienced behind the microphone. But when it comes to storytelling? We're seasoned sisters with a lifetime of practice.

We hope you'll join our circle.

What are the qualities of a good leader?

What does “workplace culture” really mean?

What is an ideal workplace culture?

title: Business Decisions and Corporate Strategy
author: Harvey Church
description:
Business Decisions and Corporate Strategy examines the choices that shape companies long before the outcome becomes obvious.
Each episode brings together multiple professional perspectives to break down a real strategic decision: what management was trying to solve, what alternatives were available, what the economics looked like, what could go wrong, and why intelligent people could reasonably disagree.
From pricing and product strategy to acquisitions, distribution, capital allocation, competitive advantage, turnarounds, and business-model shifts, the show goes beyond success stories and corporate mythology.
A good outcome does not always mean it was a good decision.
A bad outcome does not always mean it was a bad one.
The real question is whether the decision made sense with the information, incentives, risks, and constraints management had at the time.
If you want to understand how companies actually think, compete, allocate capital, and make difficult trade-offs, this is the conversation behind the headline.
